subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Scarab and the Sun
description: One-minute skill: The Scarab and the Sun.

hook.text: Egyptians watched dung beetles roll balls of dung across sand—and saw the sun being pushed across the sky.

buildup.text: The scarab beetle became Khepri, the god of the morning sun. A lowly insect embodied cosmic renewal.

discovery.text: Scarab amulets were placed over mummies' hearts. The beetle protected the dead and symbolized rebirth.

twist.text: The connection between dung and the sun seems absurd—until you realize both involve creating life from waste.

climax.text: Egypt turned the humblest creature into the symbol of creation itself. Perspective decides what's sacred.

punchline.text: A dung beetle moved the sun. Egypt believed.

quiz.question: What did the scarab beetle represent in ancient Egypt?
